topic: Simple Machines: Types, Characteristics, and Uses
key_concepts: There are six basic types of simple machines: wheel and axle, pulley, lever, inclined plan
Simple machines make work easier by changing the direction of a force or multiplying its e
Simple machines have few or no moving parts.
A lever is a rigid bar that pivots on a support called a fulcrum.
Levers increase physical force and are classified by the positions of the fulcrum, load, a
A wheelbarrow is an example of a second-class lever.
An inclined plane is a sloping surface used to move loads between areas of different heigh
Stairs, slides, ladders, and driveways are examples of inclined planes.
A wedge narrows to a thin edge and can separate, lift, or hold objects together.
A wedge is a double inclined plane sharpened at the end.
Axes, knives, and needles are examples of wedges.
A pulley uses grooved wheels and ropes or chains to raise, lower, or move a load.
